stories.title: Former garda jailed for six years over fatal hit-and-run
stories.summary: A former garda who admitted dangerous driving causing the death of a 45-year-old man in Drogheda two years ago has been jailed for six years. Niall Mac Eneaney was killed in a hit-and-run incident on the Rathmullen Road in Drogheda in the early hours of the 17 March 2024. Michael Ball previously pleaded guilty to dangerous driving causing death and failing to keep the vehicle at the scene. He was a serving garda at Drogheda Garda station at the time of the fatal hit and run.

stories.title: Fresh Wicklow searches over Dullard, Jacob disappearances
stories.summary: Gardaí investigating the disappearances of Jo Jo Dullard and Deirdre Jacob have recommenced a search operation on open ground in an area near the border between Wicklow and Kildare. The Defence Forces assisted gardaí last week - under aid to civil power arrangements - in completing a ground survey of the area in Co Wicklow. The land will now be subject to excavation and forensic examinations over the coming days. One machine at a time had been working this morning and this afternoon to meticulously search and move earth around the area, watched on by garda observers.

stories.title: Iran-US pact to halt war signed, details released 'soon'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has said an agreement with Iran ⁠has been signed and that the text of the deal would be released sometime after a formal signing on Friday, adding that the Strait of Hormuz would also be fully open. Speaking alongside French President Emmanuel Macron ahead of this week's G7 meeting, Mr Trump said ‌he did not ⁠know if he would attend the Friday ceremony expected in Geneva, but that US Vice President JD Vance would be there. "The deal is all signed. And the strait is already partially opened, as ‌you know," Mr Trump told reporters shortly after arriving in Evian, France. Mr Vance earlier said ‌the agreement had been signed digitally on Sunday and ⁠that no ‌funds were released.

stories.title: Drug dealer jailed for 10 years over threats to families
stories.summary: A 33-year-old violent drug dealer who admitted intimidating and threatening drug users and their families for money has been jailed for 10 years at the Special Criminal Court. Mark Salmon, of Kilbarron Avenue, Kilmore, Dublin, pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine he had ordered one man to collect, to organising an attack on the family home of another drug addict, threatening both families and to possession of cash and other goods that were the proceeds of crime. The offences took place over three years between 2022 and 2024. Salmon also told his victims they would be raped and murdered if they did not pay thousands of euro.

stories.title: Call for ticket revenue safeguards after Tickets.ie folds
stories.summary: Festivals left hundreds of thousands of euro out of pocket following the collapse of a major ticket agency have called for legal safeguards to protect ticket revenues. Follow the cessation of Tickets.ie, two north west festivals that took place over the June Bank Holiday weekend are owed more than €400,000 in ticket sales. The Rory Gallagher Festival in Ballyshannon in Co Donegal is owed approximately €283,000 while the Cowboys and Heroes Festival in Leitrim is owed more than €130,000 in revenue. Both festivals have initiated legal proceedings in an attempt to recover lost revenue. Tickets.ie was one of the State's largest ticketing platforms.

stories.title: Fans gather to support Pico Lopes in World Cup clash
stories.summary: Football fans have gathered in Tallaght to watch Cape Verde play Spain in their Group H World Cup opener in Atlanta as Robert 'Pico' Lopes plays for the island nation. The Shamrock Rovers captain and Crumlin native has said this is the "stuff of dreams" and that he feels like he is "representing two countries" at the World Cup. A crowd is gathering at a watch party in the Priory Market in Tallaght. Dozens of Shamrock Rovers fans were expected to support their captain as he plays for his father's home country.
